questions.q: What must reactant particles do successfully for a chemical reaction to occur between them?
a: Collide with each other with sufficient energy
Lose all of their kinetic energy

questions.q: What term describes the speed at which reactants are used up or products are formed during a chemical reaction?
How does increasing the temperature of a reaction mixture generally affect the rate of a chemical reaction?
a: It slows the reaction down completely
It has no effect on the speed
It speeds up the reaction because particles move faster and collide more frequently with more energy

questions.q: Why does increasing the concentration of a reactant in solution increase the rate of reaction?
a: It removes water from the beaker
It increases the number of reactant particles in a given volume, leading to more frequent collisions

questions.q: What happens to the rate of a reaction when a solid reactant is broken down into smaller pieces or a fine powder?
a: The rate increases because surface area is larger, allowing more collisions
The rate decreases because particles get lost

questions.q: What is a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
a: A substance that is used up permanently
A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed itself
A substance that slows down every reaction

questions.q: Which of the following describes how a catalyst works to speed up a chemical reaction?
a: By increasing the volume of the container
By providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy
By adding extra mass to the reactants

questions.q: If you increase the pressure of reacting gases, what happens to the rate of the reaction and why?
a: The rate decreases because particles spread out
The rate stays the same because gas pressure does not affect particles
The rate increases because gas particles are pushed closer together, resulting in more frequent collisions

questions.q: Which of the following factors does *not* directly affect the rate of a chemical reaction?
a: The color of the laboratory walls

questions.q: When marble chips (calcium carbonate) react with hydrochloric acid, which gas is produced, causing bubbles to form?
In an experiment measuring the rate of reaction by collecting gas, which piece of glassware is most commonly used to measure the volume of gas produced over time?
a: A gas syringe or measuring cylinder

questions.q: Why does a glowing splint pop or relight faster in pure oxygen compared to ordinary air?
a: There is less pressure in pure oxygen
The concentration of oxygen particles is higher, increasing the collision frequency

questions.q: What term is given to the minimum amount of energy that colliding particles must have for a reaction to start?
If a reaction takes 2 minutes to produce 50 cm³ of carbon dioxide gas, how could you express its average rate?
a: 25 cm³ of gas produced per minute

questions.q: Why does milk turn sour more slowly when stored inside a refrigerator compared to leaving it on a warm kitchen counter?
a: Lower temperatures reduce particle kinetic energy and collision frequency, slowing down the spoiling reactions

questions.q: Which of the following reactions would you expect to proceed the fastest at room temperature?
a: The rusting of an iron bridge over several years
The weathering of rock over centuries

questions.q: How does particle theory explain why crushed chalk reacts much faster with acid than a single large lump of chalk?
a: Crushing exposes more surface area, exposing more particles to collisions with acid molecules
Crushing turns chalk into a gas

questions.q: Biological catalysts found in living organisms that speed up vital chemical reactions are called what?
When investigating the effect of temperature on reaction rate, what variable must be kept constant to ensure a fair test?
a: The concentration and volume of the acid used

questions.q: What happens to the mass of a reaction flask if a gas is allowed to escape freely into the air during the reaction?
a: The total mass decreases as the gas escapes

questions.q: Why do wood shavings catch fire and burn much faster than a heavy solid log of wood?
a: Shavings have a greater surface area exposed to oxygen
Shavings are made of a different chemical element

questions.q: What is meant by a 'successful collision' between reactant particles?
a: Any collision that causes particles to bounce off
A collision that has sufficient energy and correct orientation to result in a chemical reaction
A collision that produces heat without changing chemicals
A collision between solvent molecules only

questions.q: During a chemical reaction over time, what happens to the rate of the reaction as the reactants get used up?
a: It stays constant until the end
It slows down and eventually stops

questions.q: Which of these devices can be placed under a reaction flask on a balance to automatically record mass loss as gas escapes over time?
a: A data logger connected to an electronic balance

questions.q: Why does adding a catalyst not get used up or consumed permanently during a chemical reaction?
a: It provides a pathway but is regenerated unchanged at the end of the reaction
It does not interact with particles at all

questions.q: How does lowering the temperature affect the rate at which food spoils or bacteria multiply?
If you dilute an acid solution with a large amount of water, what happens to the rate of its reaction with magnesium ribbon?
a: The reaction rate decreases because there are fewer acid particles per unit volume

questions.q: What is collision theory used to explain in chemistry?
a: How chemical reactions occur and why different factors affect reaction rates

questions.q: In a graph showing the volume of gas produced against time, what does a steeper initial slope indicate?
a: A faster initial rate of reaction

questions.q: Why are grain elevators or flour mills dangerous places where dust explosions can occur?
a: Fine flour dust has a huge surface area and can burn with explosive speed when mixed with air and a spark

questions.q: What happens when manganese(IV) oxide is added to hydrogen peroxide solution during a school demonstration?
a: It acts as a catalyst to speed up the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen

questions.q: Which of the following conditions would yield the fastest reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid?
a: Zinc powder in dilute acid at 15°C
Zinc powder in concentrated hydrochloric acid at 50°C

questions.q: If a reaction graph flattens out into a horizontal line at 60 cm³ after 4 minutes, what does the horizontal section signify?
a: The reaction has stopped because at least one reactant is completely used up
Gas is being created faster than ever

questions.q: Why does a car engine run efficiently only when fuel is atomized (sprayed into a fine mist) before ignition?
a: To increase surface area for rapid and complete combustion
To prevent any reaction from happening

questions.q: According to collision theory, why do particles react faster when heated?
a: They gain kinetic energy, move faster, collide more frequently, and more particles exceed the activation energy

questions.q: What is the primary role of catalysts in industrial chemical processes like making ammonia or margarine?
a: To increase the cost of production
To save energy and time by allowing reactions to occur faster at lower temperatures and pressures

questions.q: Which of the following changes would decrease the rate of reaction between magnesium ribbon and dilute sulfuric acid?
a: Diluting the acid with extra water
Using magnesium powder instead of a ribbon

questions.q: In a closed container, what happens to the frequency of collisions between gas particles if the volume of the container is reduced?
What is a major visual sign that a chemical reaction rate can be measured by observing a precipitate form?
a: A clear solution turns cloudy or opaque over time

questions.q: Why do food packages often include small packets labeled 'Do Not Eat' containing iron powder and silica gel?
a: To add flavor to the food
To absorb moisture and oxygen, slowing down oxidation and spoiling reactions
